rule: w_market = max(0, L0 − L_market) / (max(0, L0 − L_model) + max(0, L0 − L_market)); blended = (1 − w_market)·model + w_market·market
model_beats_coin_flip_note: the model's out-of-sample log-loss on the settled sample is WORSE than a coin flip — the rule below therefore gives the market the whole weight as soon as the market demonstrates any skill at all, which is the honest answer, not a defect in the rule
market_log_loss_reason: no closing line exists in any committed capture — requirement R-043 / R-101, flagged F-V4-04 in the v4 capture index
w_market_reason: undefined until a closing line is captured and scored out-of-sample — no closing line exists in any committed capture — requirement R-043 / R-101, flagged F-V4-04 in the v4 capture index
blended_margin_reason: a blend needs a market number; with no closing line the blend would be the model number wearing a market label

measurements.leakage_rule: ratings for a date use only games strictly before that date
measurements.official_source: data/raw/history/*.json — 183 official finals, one nba.com/game URL per row

measurements.sample: sealed ledgers settled against official finals
measurements.leakage_rule: predictions were sealed (sha256) before tip and verified unmodified at settlement
measurements.calibration_read: 12 correct winners in 14 distinct games is a hit rate of 0.857 against 0.633 expected under the seals' own probabilities. The Poisson-binomial tail (p_at_least_observed_hits) is the only honest yardstick: below 0.05 the run is outside the noise band, but on 14 games in one week it is not a measured edge, it is not staked, and the bet surface still publishes zero rows.

grid_note: Every row is the pre-registered rule evaluated at a hypothetical market log-loss. It is arithmetic on the stated formula, not a measurement: no market log-loss has been observed, because no closing price exists in any committed capture.
grid_reads: Because the model currently shows no skill against a coin flip on the settled sample, the rule gives the market the entire weight for any market log-loss below the baseline. That is the rule working as pre-registered, and it is a statement about the sample (22 graded games), not a proof about the model.
what_would_unblock_it: A licensed odds feed capturing the closing spread, total and moneyline per game with a stated timestamp policy (R-101).
A decision on storage and display terms for those prices (open question on the Decisions needed page).
At least one full out-of-sample window of market log-loss scored on the same games as the model, so the two numbers are comparable.
